title: A common affine open with a generically geometrically integral hypersurface
statement: Let X be reduced affine, S integral affine [def-pc-integral-scheme], and f:X\to S flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let \eta be a generic point of S. Suppose X_\eta [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Put A=\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S). There exist an affine open W\subseteq X, n\in\mathbf N, and P\in A[t_1,\ldots,t_n] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] such that \eta lies in the image of W\to S and there is an open immersion i:W\to H [def-weil-open-immersion], where H=\operatorname{Spec}(A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(P)) [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. If g:H\to S is the map induced by the coefficient inclusion and the canonical affine identification S\cong\operatorname{Spec}A, then i followed by g is f restricted to W, and H_\eta is geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced. No special-fibre assertion is made.

source.place: Tag 0559, lemma-geometrically-irreducible-generic-fibre, first proof, separating transcendence basis and common-open paragraphs; Tag 0552, Lemma 29.51.7

proof.text: Apply the generic-fibre birational hypersurface model theorem to obtain n, P, geometric irreducibility and reducedness of the hypersurface generic fibre, and a partial isomorphism of the generic fibres over the generic residue field.

The quotient of the finite-variable polynomial algebra by its principal ideal is finitely presented over the base global sections. Therefore the hypersurface map g is locally of finite presentation. Generic geometric irreducibility makes the source generic fibre nonempty. Apply the spreading theorem to the partial isomorphism to get an open V in X meeting the generic fibre and an open immersion V into H over S.

Choose v in V mapping to eta. The affine-open basis gives an affine open W containing v and contained in V. Compose its inclusion into V with the open immersion into H. Composition preserves open immersions and the equation over S, while v witnesses eta in the image of W. Retain the two geometric properties of the hypersurface generic fibre from the first step.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_common_generic_hypersurface_affine_open
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsReduced X] [IsAffine S] [IsIntegral S]
    (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (η : S) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ)
    (hgeom : GeometricallyIrreducible (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η))
    (hred : GeometricallyReduced (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)) :
    ∃ W : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen W ∧ η ∈ Set.range (W.ι ≫ f) ∧
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (P : MvPolynomial (Fin n) Γ(S, ⊤)),
        let H := Spec (.of (MvPolynomial (Fin n) Γ(S, ⊤) ⧸ Ideal.span {P}))
        let g : H ⟶ S := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {P})).comp MvPolynomial.C)) ≫ S.isoSpec.inv
        ∃ i : W.toScheme ⟶ H, IsOpenImmersion i ∧ i ≫ g = W.ι ≫ f ∧
          GeometricallyIrreducible (g.fiberToSpecResidueField η) ∧
          GeometricallyReduced (g.fiberToSpecResidueField η)
